To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Renaissance was not the age of religious skepticism, that the Catholic Reformation was not the product of the Renaissance, and that the Reformation was not a major factor in the Catholic Reformation (1).
the Catholic reform of the sixteenth century was more than a reaction to the Protestant Reformation and that it was a movement with many dimensions.
Catholicism was refashioned in the sixteenth century in ways that made it a more vital and effective religion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between religion and culture in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
the nature of Catholicism during the Renaissance. We are not concerned with a single, unified Catholicism, but rather with the variety
how and to what extent the Catholic Church was able to maintain and renew its identity in the face of a number of challenges.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Renaissance was neither a secular age nor a pagan one; that it was a time of intense religious activity and concern; that it was an age in which religious ideas and practices were being transformed; that it was the time when the Reformation and Counter-Reformation began.
the Catholicism of the sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries was not so much a religion of faith as one of works.
Catholicism, far from being in decline, was in the sixteenth century a dynamic and growing force.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

religion in the sixteenth century was not as important in the lives of individuals as it was in the fifteenth, that the Church was not as important to the life of society as it was in 1500, and that the Church was more important to the state in 1600 than it had been a hundred years before (p. 3).
religion was more important to the Renaissance than Burckhardt thought, and less important than the Counter-Reformation made it out to be.
the Catholic Reformation was not a single event, not a simple phenomenon, and not a movement with a clear-cut program or a single leader.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Catholicism, as the religion of the vast majority of people, was a powerful force in Renaissance society. It shaped their lives and
the Catholic Reformation, the reform of the Catholic Church, was the most important development in the religious history of the period.
religion is not something that is simply there to be studied as a part of culture.
